Longitudinal data object for LMTP analyses

LMTPData.Rd

LMTPData is an R6 class that provides structure to longitudinal causal data organized as baseline covariates W, time-varying covariates L_t, treatments A_t, and a final outcome Y.

It provides convenient methods to extract per-time histories H_t, treatments, outcomes, and related longitudinal views used throughout {modulatR}.

The object is intentionally structural rather than algorithmic: it stores the node layout and exposes standardized views of the observed data, but it does not itself perform nuisance estimation, imputation, or targeting.

Public fields

id_col

Name of the unit identifier column.

A_cols

Character vector of treatment column names.

L_cols

List of character vectors giving time-varying covariates at each time point.

W_cols

Optional character vector of baseline covariate names.

Y_col

Outcome column name.

metadata

Optional list of additional metadata.

Active bindings

n

Number of rows in the data.

p

Number of columns in the underlying data.

colnames

Column names of the underlying data.

Examples

## Single timepoint example (tau = 1)
n <- 100
df <- tibble::tibble(
  `L[t1,1]` = rnorm(n), `L[t1,2]` = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5),
  A = rbinom(n, 1, plogis(0.4 + `L[t1,1]` + `L[t1,2]`)),
  Y = rnorm(n, mean = `L[t1,2]` + 2.3*A, sd = .1))
ds <- LMTPData$new(
  data = df,
  L_cols = list(c('L[t1,2]', 'L[t1,2]')),
  A_cols = 'A',
  Y_col = 'Y')
ds
#> LMTPData
#>   n: 100
#>   tau: 1
#>   id: ..row_id
#>   W: <none>
#>   A: A
#>   Y: Y
#>   L by time:
#>     t = 1: L[t1,2], L[t1,2]

## Two-timepoint example (tau = 2)
df <- data.frame(
  id = 1:n,
  W1 = rnorm(n),
  L1 = rnorm(n),
  A1 = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5),
  L2 = rnorm(n),
  A2 = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5),
  Y  = rnorm(n)
)

ds <- LMTPData$new(
  data = df,
  id_col = "id",
  A_cols = c("A1", "A2"),
  L_cols = list(
    "L1",
    "L2"
  ),
  W_cols = "W1",
  Y_col = "Y"
)

ds
#> LMTPData
#>   n: 100
#>   tau: 2
#>   id: id
#>   W: W1
#>   A: A1, A2
#>   Y: Y
#>   L by time:
#>     t = 1: L1
#>     t = 2: L2

# Histories
head(ds$H(1))  # (W, L1)
#>   id         W1         L1
#> 1  1 -1.0644642 -0.8452478
#> 2  2  1.0771165 -0.9615715
#> 3  3  1.1815756  1.0174911
#> 4  4  0.1983921 -1.4960537
#> 5  5 -0.4004052 -1.1848187
#> 6  6  0.6161543  0.6302344
head(ds$H(2))  # (W, L1, L2, A1)
#>   id         W1         L1 A1         L2
#> 1  1 -1.0644642 -0.8452478  1 -0.9531239
#> 2  2  1.0771165 -0.9615715  1  1.7927561
#> 3  3  1.1815756  1.0174911  1  0.3489767
#> 4  4  0.1983921 -1.4960537  0  0.2591038
#> 5  5 -0.4004052 -1.1848187  1 -0.8059519
#> 6  6  0.6161543  0.6302344  0  0.1056647

# Treatment at time 2
head(ds$A(2))
#> [1] 0 0 1 0 0 1
head(ds$AH(2))
#>   id         W1         L1 A1         L2 A2
#> 1  1 -1.0644642 -0.8452478  1 -0.9531239  0
#> 2  2  1.0771165 -0.9615715  1  1.7927561  0
#> 3  3  1.1815756  1.0174911  1  0.3489767  1
#> 4  4  0.1983921 -1.4960537  0  0.2591038  0
#> 5  5 -0.4004052 -1.1848187  1 -0.8059519  0
#> 6  6  0.6161543  0.6302344  0  0.1056647  1
